items.claim: When `compdef` is not defined, the sourced script still falls through to `_rg "$@"`, so the newly documented `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` fails if it runs before `compinit` (or without it), and the FAQ never states that ordering requirement.
items.consequence: A user puts `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` in .zshrc above `compinit` or the oh-my-zsh source line (or runs it in `zsh -f`). `$+functions[compdef]` is 0, so `_rg` runs outside any completion widget and prints an error such as `command not found: _arguments` on every shell start, and no completion is registered. This is the same class of failure as issue #2956, with no hint that compinit must come first.

items.claim: The snippet the FAQ says to add to `$HOME/.zshrc` carries a `$ ` shell-prompt prefix, unlike the `fpath=` snippet just above it that targets the same file.
items.consequence: A user copies the block verbatim into ~/.zshrc as instructed. Every shell start then prints `zsh: command not found: $` and completions are never loaded.

items.claim: The new `fpath=($HOME/.zsh-complete $fpath)` instruction omits that it must come before `compinit` runs, and that `compinit` must run at all.
items.consequence: A user appends the fpath line to the end of ~/.zshrc, after `compinit` or `source $ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh`. compinit has already scanned the old fpath, so `_rg` is never registered and the 'recommended approach' silently does nothing, which is the gap the reviewer asked to close in thread 9.

items.claim: Using `$funcstack[1] == _rg` as the 'am I being autoloaded' test regresses any setup where the file body runs under another name while `compdef` exists, and misfires the other way when a file literally named `_rg` is sourced.
items.consequence: (a) The file is installed in fpath as e.g. `_ripgrep` (its `#compdef rg` tag still registers it), or is sourced from inside a wrapper or lazy-loader function: funcstack[1] is not `_rg` and compdef exists, so the first TAB only runs `compdef _rg rg` and returns no matches, where it previously completed. (b) `cd ~/.zsh-complete && source _rg` in an interactive shell: funcstack[1] is likely the bare name `_rg`, so `_rg "$@"` runs and reproduces the original `_arguments:comparguments: can only be called from completion function` error.

items.claim: The `(( ! $+functions[compdef] ))` clause exists only to keep `ci/test-complete` working, so it conflates 'test harness' with 'user has no compinit' instead of keying on the existing `_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS` signal, and the comment above it does not explain the clause.
items.consequence: Run `ci/test-complete` where zsh startup files define `compdef` (e.g. compinit or a plugin-manager stub in ~/.zshenv, which `#!/usr/bin/env zsh` scripts read). `( _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source $1 )` takes the else branch, prints nothing, and the script fails with 'Failed to get comp_args'. Checking `_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS` explicitly, or having the test call `_rg` itself, would fix this and allow a clear message or no-op when compdef is absent (finding 1).

items.claim: No test covers the new branch: nothing checks that sourcing the script with `compdef` defined registers `_rg` for `rg` without invoking it.
items.consequence: A later edit to the trailer (e.g. simplifying the condition back to `_rg "$@"` or changing the funcstack check) re-breaks `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`. CI stays green because `test-complete` only exercises the compdef-absent path.

items.claim: The new caveat sentence is ungrammatical: 'while this approach is easier to setup, is generally slower' lacks a subject, and 'setup' should be the verb 'set up'.
items.consequence: User-facing documentation reads as broken; it should say 'while this approach is easier to set up, it is generally slower than the previous method'.

items.claim: Promoting `source <(...)` means the completion functions are parsed under the interactive shell's aliases and options, whereas compinit's `autoload -U` path suppresses alias expansion.
items.consequence: A user has a regular or global alias matching a word used in `_rg`, `_rg_types` or `_rg_encodings`. With the sourced method the alias is expanded into the function bodies at definition time and completion misbehaves, while the same script in fpath works. This is speculative and generic to sourced completions; it would be cheap to note in the FAQ caveat.
